input.candidate_text:
Let \(m=(p-1)/2=2t+1\), which is odd.

Suppose first that \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\). Then \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=p-1=2m\). Hence \(a^{2m}\equiv1\pmod p\), while \(a^m\not\equiv1\pmod p\). Since \((a^m)^2\equiv1\pmod p\) and \(p\) is prime, it follows that \(a^m\equiv-1\pmod p\). Because \(m\) is odd,
\[
(-a)^m=(-1)^m a^m\equiv(-1)(-1)\equiv1\pmod p.
\]
If \((-a)^n\equiv1\pmod p\), then \(a^{2n}=(-a)^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p\). Thus \(2m\mid2n\), so \(m\mid n\). Therefore \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)=m=(p-1)/2\).

Conversely, suppose \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)=m\), and put \(b=-a\). Then \(b^m\equiv1\pmod p\). Since \(m\) is odd,
\[
a^m=(-b)^m\equiv-1\pmod p,
\]
so \(a^{2m}\equiv1\pmod p\). Now suppose \(a^n\equiv1\pmod p\). Then \(b^{2n}=a^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p\), and hence \(m\mid2n\). As \(m\) is odd, \(m\mid n\); write \(n=qm\). We then have
\[
1\equiv a^n=(a^m)^q\equiv(-1)^q\pmod p.
\]
Because \(p\) is odd, \(q\) must be even. Consequently \(2m\mid n\). Since \(a^{2m}\equiv1\pmod p\), this proves \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=2m=p-1\). Thus \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\).

problem.theorem: Consider a prime $p$ of the form $4 t+3$. Show that $a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ iff $-a$ has order $(p-1) / 2$.
